samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Written as a fake email thread among University of Scranton faculty, the appendix has junior professor Joe Kraus propose reading the town through Baudrillard's simulacrum - the 'Scranton Welcomes You' sign from the credits becoming real for him only as a TV image - while senior colleagues tutor him through the history of representation theory. Stephen deploys Plato's Ion (Socrates' magnet-and-iron chain of imitation, with Ion's Brent-like obliviousness) and Aristotle on mimesis, pity, fear, and catharsis to explain the show's tragicomic discomfort, while Maria adds the Antiochene, Alexandrian, and Augustinian fourfold senses of scripture applied to Scranton; Michael Friedman contributes a Chekhovian reading of Pam's bird eulogy as subtext about Michael's fear of dying alone. The thread itself mirrors an Office plotline as the senior faculty quietly decide to cut the untenured Joe out of the project.

samples.book: 109 - Mr. Robot and Philosophy - Beyond Good and Evil Corp
samples.title: 2. If I Don’t Listen to My Imaginary Friend, Why the Fuck Should I Listen to Yours
samples.relation: Kreider stages a chat between Plato and Aristotle about the show. On Plato's account, mimesis is an imitation of an imitation of the Forms, so Elliot's imaginary friend, his fake persona with Krista, and the Mr. Robot personality are intellectually and morally dangerous deceptions that let him commit terrorism without his rational self's consent; yet the Republic's censored poetry for the auxiliaries explains how fsociety's masked videos teach true beliefs, and how Elliot uses the fictional Mr. Robot to educate himself toward ideas he already knew were right. Aristotle's Poetics then defends imitation as natural and instructive - the show is a cautionary tragedy, and the Mr. Robot crutch is how Elliot eventually steps up to claim responsibility.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Sacrificial Lamb
samples.relation: Argues Astro Boy re-enacts the sacrificial logic of the atomic age: Atomu is the nuclear-powered copy of the dead Tobio, born from Dr. Tenma's refusal to accept mortality, and his repeated self-sacrifice for humans who discard him (as in 'Save the Classmate,' where the rescued boys' parents still want him removed) shows him functioning as Heidegger's 'standing-reserve' — an object valued only as stored power, with humans themselves next in line. Drawing on Plato's Republic anxiety over originals and copies, Adorno and Horkheimer's dialectic of enlightenment, and Rey Chow's account of mimesis as the sign left by sacrifice, the chapter reads the series as mourning an innocence that became impossible after Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

samples.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
samples.title: 13. The Laughter and the Fury
samples.relation: Situates Inside Amy Schumer between Aristotle's Poetics dictum that valor in a woman is inappropriate, his Politics claim of female inferiority, and the 1970s French feminists: Cixous's 'Laugh of the Medusa' breaking up truth with laughter and Irigaray's strategic mimesis. Kolb reads stereotype-performing sketches with violent endings, such as the 'I'm So Bad' women devouring a waiter's face and the 'You Are Gorgeous' anthem rewarding a faked miscarriage and an N-word rap, as resubmitting women to stereotypes to explode them. Casting-couch opener '2 Girls, 1 Cup', 'Focus Group', and '12 Angry Men' hold up a mirror to the male gaze and to the rage it produces when women stop performing for it.

samples.book: 064 - The Rolling Stones and Philosophy - It's Just a Thought Away
samples.title: Exile from Ancient Greece—Yeah!
samples.relation: Answers the anti-relativist who holds Main Street's greatness self-explanatory: if its meaning has nothing to do with what Liz Phair thinks, it has nothing to do with what the fundamentalist thinks either. The skeptics' error—expecting Guyville to sound like Main Street—inherits the Platonic-Aristotelian assumption that inspiration means imitation (knowing a statue's beauty means containing a copy of its shape), whereas the Stones themselves 'responded' to Muddy Waters and Chuck Berry without merely imitating; Phair's closer 'Strange Loop,' its riff morphing into '6’1”,' closes the hermeneutic circle and invites us to revisit, not finalize, Exile.

samples.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
samples.title: 8. What Are You Hearing
samples.relation: Wissner shows how Twilight Zone scores mark the boundary between dream and reality: electronic instruments and reverberation in 'Perchance to Dream' (Hammond organ, Theremin-like violin), diegetic folk songs against the Willoughby theme in 'A Stop at Willoughby,' the shared recurring nightmare cue of 'Twenty-Two' and 'Shadow Play,' and the desperate piano ostinato of 'The Midnight Sun.' Framing this with Plato's view of music as unreal, image-evoking mimetic signs and Aristotle's claim that melodies carry ethos and can change minds, she argues music tells viewers what pictures cannot: whether a character is dreaming, imagining, or awake.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Mackey tracks the ontological migrations of Lyra, Pantalaimon, and the alethiometer from black marks on a page into the Listening Library audiobook with fixed voices, the National Theatre's puppet dæmons whose black-clad puppeteer stunningly turns out to speak as Lyra's death, the film's computer-graphic Pan with its explanatory opening voice-over, the dæmon-assignment website, a videogame that reduces Pan's shape-shifting to four player-chosen forms, and a Tonner collectible doll with a resin Pantalaimon. She asks whether 'reinforced fiction' supported by extratextual evidence (publisher websites, playbill portraits supposedly showing historical dæmons) makes stories feel more real, and what essential qualities make each embodied version still count as Lyra or Pan. Her conclusion is a research program: understanding how readers conjure fictional beings 'out of all air and thought' across media would be a giant step toward understanding the intricacies of the human mind.

samples.book: 118 - Scott Adams and Philosophy - A Hole in the Fabric of Reality
samples.title: 13. The Essence of Dogbert
samples.relation: Knuths asks whether Dogbert is essentially a dog and only accidentally white, importing Aristotle's Metaphysics distinction between essential and accidental properties and its modern modal gloss: essences are what an object has in all possible worlds, with David Lewis's concrete-constructionist reading noted against the standard view of worlds as abstract sets of propositions. The puzzle is that Dogbert's 2014 stint as CEO, combined with his canine essence, would prove dogs can be CEOs, threatening absurd conclusions about the real world unless we choose an ontology of fiction. Three candidates are weighed without a verdict: possibilism (Adams discovered a possible world), Meinongianism (Dogbert has being without existence, at the cost of square circles), and creationism (Dogbert is Adams's abstract artifact, troubled by the Not-Adams duplicate-creator case).

samples.book: 191 - Star Wars and Philosophy Strikes Back - This Is the Way
samples.title: “Master Skywalker. There Are Too Many of Them. What Are We Going to Do ”
samples.relation: Cook and Kellen ask what makes the Luke of A New Hope the same fictional character as the Luke of The Last Jedi, the Thrawn Trilogy, or fan fiction like Old Man Luke. They reject sameness of name, Leibniz's identity of indiscernibles (Luke_ANH lacks Luke_TLJ's internal properties such as being a jaded Jedi Master), and the authorial say-so account of Routley and Thomasson, which by transitivity forces the contradiction that Zahn's married, child-having Luke is identical to the Last Jedi recluse who never met Mara Jade. They defend a 'Perspectival Account' on which identity claims are true or false only relative to the story from which we interpret them, so each viewing of A New Hope shows innumerably many distinct yet connected Lukes - 'ontological excess' spanning canon, Legends, Infinities, and the Muppet Show.

samples.book: 059 - Halo and Philosophy - Intellect Evolved
samples.title: Sound, Music, and Vision
samples.relation: Ben Abraham asks why Halo 2's music cannot keep up with a speedrun like Cody Miller's: Martin O'Donnell's pre-composed, linear scores have only an accidental 'forced marriage' with unpredictable player action, and cinematic scoring (the Psycho shower scene) would demand sacrificing agency as Guitar Hero and Rez do. Surveying definitions of music—Plato's song of words, mode, and rhythm in Republic Book 2, Schafer's Apollonian versus Dionysian origin myths, and African and gamelan challenges to the Western score-centered 'work'—he argues the incompatibility dissolves if music is redefined broadly. Halo 2's sound effects turn out to be secretly musical: the Covenant carbine's zoom sounds a perfect fourth (G-flat to D-flat), the plasma pistol charges to B-flat—pitched, rhythmic design already synchronized to onscreen action, bridging music and interactivity.

samples.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
samples.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
samples.relation: Joel McIver, drawing on years of interviewing the band, argues the sinister sound is psychoacoustics rather than Satan: Iommi's lower tuning adopted after the sheet-metal press took his fingertips, the tritone or diabolus in musica that anchors "Black Sabbath", horror-film tremolo, minor keys, Ozzy's untrained monotone, and Bill Ward's slightly dragged, jazzy beats, artistic imperfections that keep the music lifelike. Against Schopenhauer's view that music directly expresses universal emotions, so the tritone would naturally sound like discord to anyone, McIver contends the devil's interval is a Western convention that only became inseparable from evil once Sabbath fused it with Geezer's occult lyrics and nightmare cover art.

samples.book: 195 - Ted Lasso and Philosophy - No Question Is Into Touch
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Belluomini argues the show's score and soundtrack do genuine aesthetic and moral work, applying Aristotle's Politics Book VIII claim that music imitates emotion and disposes us toward virtue. He analyzes Celeste's 'Strange' narrating the divorce-signing and intercut romances, 'Wise Up' underscoring Rebecca's brave break with John Wingsnight, 'Piano Joint' carrying Rebecca's confession to Ted, 'She's a Rainbow' scoring Roy's run back to Nelson Road, 'Roy Walk Off' as a Jaws-style sentimental motif, and 'Spiegel im Spiegel' under Rebecca's anti-Super-League speech, closing with Schopenhauer's point that fitting music is a scene's most accurate commentary.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Football as Part of Real Life
samples.relation: Hoyningen-Huene asks why anyone cheers a ball crossing an arbitrarily defined line and answers with his thesis that football re-enacts the drama of life: an unpredictable, fractal mixture of ability and chance—from a bobbling pitch to Manchester United's 1999 injury-time comeback and Maradona's unpunished Hand of God—mirroring the luck, skill, and irreversible injustice of real life. He analyzes the Laws of the Game as having four functions: guaranteeing equal conditions, generating analogies to life's drama, ending the drama at a knowable moment (unlike life's open-ended conflicts), and keeping the game safely distanced from real seriousness, which is why he reads hooligans as people who cognitively mistake the game's drama for a real-life fight. Finally he argues that money, careers, betting, and even the political channeling of Hungary's 1954 World Cup defeat into the 1956 uprising are secondary entanglements parasitic on a primary fascination already present in a nameless village-league match, which no other sport matches in variability of the ability–chance mixture.

samples.book: 041 - Stephen Colbert and Philosophy - I Am Philosophy (And So Can You!)
samples.title: Sin, Play, and the “Synagogues of Satan”
samples.relation: Rachael Sotos argues the Report performs Platonic play: like the divine puppet of Plato's Laws with its competing cords, Colbert reveals what moves us (fear, hope, the ThreatDown bears, the 'golden cord' of the good) and so teaches freedom through play. Colbert's pompous self-authority - claiming to be 'the canon and measure' of virtue in I Am America - parodies Aristotle's serious man (spoudaios, megalopsychos) and the sophists Protagoras and Prodicus with their Orpheus voices, proving Heraclitus right that 'time is a child at play' and Aristotle wrong that play is mere medicinal rest. Tracking the war on fun from Chrysostom through Aquinas's eutrapelia (there is sin in a lack of play) to Erasmus's Praise of Folly and the Puritans' ban on theaters as 'Synagogues of Satan,' she reads Colbert's playing-at-sin - the man-seed eugenics bit, the 'black friend' boasts, the Ellen DeGeneres Paradox on Wikiality - as Erasmian folly that heals America's Puritan hangover in the culture wars.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a12.xhtml
samples.relation: O'Hara argues that play is what makes hobbits - and us - fully human: Bilbo's childhood games of throwing stones, riddles and smoke-rings turn out to be training for the quest (his stone-throwing fells the spiders, his riddle-practice buys time with Gollum), and even Gollum's riddle-game makes him momentarily 'less a monster and more a person'. Following Schiller's and Huizinga's Homo ludens thesis that play completes humanity, he distinguishes play from idleness (Aquinas held recreation continues in heaven; Peirce called play 'vigorous exercise'), places leisure among the goods of Aristotle's 'we play in order to be serious', and contrasts Gandalf's beauty-directed fireworks with the orcs' merely useful explosions and work-chants. But play has limits: Kant warns against treating persons as toys, and Bilbo's lesson is 'Never laugh at live dragons!'

samples.book: 185 - Saturday Night Live and Philosophy - Deep Thoughts Through the Decades
samples.title: “We’re Not Worthy”
samples.relation: Holt reads Wayne's World as applied philosophy of play: Wayne and Garth's basement show is intrinsically motivated leisure in Huizinga's sense, free, rule-bound, absorbing, and outside ordinary life, and Russell's 'In Praise of Idleness' supplies the play ethic against the work ethic. Against Wittgenstein's claim that games cannot be defined, Suits's definition of games as the voluntary attempt to overcome unnecessary obstacles is applied to 'A-sphincter-says-what?', the '...not!' game, and one-on-one hockey with Gretzky. The dark side of play closes the chapter: Wayne and Garth exclude and mock outsiders, and the leisure of their magic circle rests on unacknowledged labor like Wayne's mom's laundry.

samples.book: 211 - Golf and Philosophy - Lessons from the Links
samples.title: First Hole Golf and the Importance of Play
samples.relation: Al Gini defends play as intrinsically valuable and essential to being human, drawing on Huizinga's three criteria of 'true play' and William James's ideal of the amateur who plays 'for the love of it.' Using his golf-obsessed father as an extended case, he shows how golf functions as a self-contained, absorbing 'refuge from ordinary life' that delivers completion, coordination, and cooperation, echoing Plato's claim in the Republic and Laws that sport forms both person and community. The chapter treats golf as an end in itself whose joy sustains a flourishing life rather than as a means to external reward.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Wave Goodbye from the Catbus
samples.relation: Heinricy argues anime is the richest medium for posthuman theory because it shows bodies 'in a state of becoming' rather than as grotesque boundary violations: Miyazaki's Catbus and Totoro, Haku's dragon transformation and Chihiro's pig parents in Spirited Away, and the cursed pig-headed aviator of Porco Rosso all treat morphing bodies as possibility, not horror. She sorts anime posthumanism into two valences: a 'Ghost in the Machine' dream of consciousness leaving the body altogether (Motoko merging with the net in Ghost in the Shell), which she rebuts via N. Katherine Hayles's point that consciousness is embodied and would change with any new body, and hybrid configurations like mecha (Gundam, Robotech) where body and machine drive each other. Following Donna Haraway, she contends we are all already cyborgs — vaccines, engineered food, treated water — and credits Japan's nuclear history (via Susan Napier) and its shape-shifting folklore for why anime embraces rather than fears the transformed body.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Caroline Mosser treats the creature's tragedy as humanist prejudice rather than necessity: the blind De Lacey accepts the eloquent creature sight unseen, so he passes Alan Turing's test, and only the sighted family's terror at his body rejects him - bias against the artificial, not reason. She reads the creature's development through fire, language, and revolution as Rousseau's progression from natural innocence to corruption by society, and Donna Haraway's cyborg as the figure he prefigures: an unfaithful illegitimate offspring who rebels against his father and undermines patriarchal Western self/other dualisms. The chapter concludes that society cannot accept enhanced or posthuman beings until it finds a middle ground beyond its binary grids of good/bad and Self/Other, since otherwise any new life we create will be Othered, hated, and oppressed like Frankenstein's.

samples.book: 102 - Orphan Black and Philosophy - Grand Theft DNA
samples.title: 13. Sisterhood’s Back in Orphan Black
samples.relation: Recounts the rise and fall of second-wave sisterhood — the dream of a unified female voice that erased differences of race, class, sexuality, and nation until the 1980s backlash killed it — and argues Orphan Black resurrects a corrected version through Rosi Braidotti's posthumanism. The clones, disposable bodies of biogenetic capitalism, build a sisterhood that celebrates difference (grunge Sarah, dreads-and-lab-coat Cosima, suburban Alison, savage Helena) rather than enforcing sameness, and that welcomes the Others the Seventies excluded — gay Felix, Black Art, Hindu Raj — while white Western men like Paul remain the surveillance agents of the backlash. Through posthumanism's dissolution of fixed human identity, the chapter claims, feminism's old ideal returns both transformed and inclusive.

samples.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
samples.title: 7. More Human than Humans
samples.relation: Rob O'Connor reads replicants through N. Katherine Hayles's posthumanism — persons as amalgams of biological and informational-technological systems — arguing Rachael's procreation shows the posthuman body bypassing its designed limits, while Joi is a posthuman of the opposite construction, a hologram transcending her limits through emotion. Memory and experience, even implanted ones (Batty's 'tears in rain', Deckard's unicorn dream, K's wooden horse, 'all the best memories are hers'), supply the existential context that defines the posthuman self. K's epiphany before the giant Joi advertisement reveals he is a tool of the capitalist system, and his choice to die for the right cause is how he takes charge of his own identity.

samples.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
samples.title: From Self-Alienation to Posthumanism The Transmigration of the Burroughsian Subject
samples.relation: Bolton argues William S. Burroughs's fragmented subjects—split by a parasitic 'Other Half' or word virus—are not postmodernism's dissolved nonsubjects but practitioners of a productive self-alienation. He aligns Burroughs's multiply-named, body-swapping characters (Mr. Bradley Mr. Martin, Joe the Dead) with Lacan's split subject constituted in language and with Derrida's iterable 'mark' and 'third that walks beside you' as an absent-present that dissolves binaries. Through Naked Lunch, Nova Express, and The Western Lands the Burroughsian subject transmigrates from Marxian/Hegelian alienation to N. Katherine Hayles's posthuman, gaining agency by extending into its technologized environment.

samples.book: 128 - Mister Rogers and Philosophy - Wondering through the Neighborhood
samples.title: 13. Won’t You Be My Posthuman Neighbor
samples.relation: Fernando Pagnoni Berns reads the show as posthumanist: the toy-model opening credits leave it unclear whether Rogers himself is a toy, Trolley refuses orange juice yet speaks (an object with a will), Lady Aberlin uses a bass as a dance partner, and Audrey Duck's 'You're as real as you want to be' collapses human, animal, and hand puppet. Invoking Bruno Latour's quasi-human 'non-humans' that channel human desires, he argues the Neighborhood dissolves the humanist hierarchy that enthrones the white Western male over women, animals, objects, and plants.

samples.book: 063 - Philip K. Dick and Philosophy - Do Androids Have Kindred Spirits
samples.title: And the Next Step
samples.relation: Surveys science fiction's next-step humanity — Wells's genetically stratified future, Stapledon's successions of human forms, and the Campbell-era optimism Dick resisted — then turns to contemporary 'posthumanist' theorists like Donna Haraway who want 'human,' 'natural,' and 'gender' fluidly redefined. Dick emerges as the voice of caution in this cross-pollination: expand the definition of what human means, but not at the cost of the compassion and empathy that make us human.

samples.book: 222 - The Philosophy of Horror
samples.title: The ageing woman as (American) horror story
samples.relation: The chapter theorises the 'abject barren body' — the menstruating, menopausal and post-menopausal woman — connecting menarche as an upswell of feminine power (Carrie's telekinesis, Ginger Snaps, The Witch's Thomasin) to menopause's cultural construction as loss and 'living decay'. Drawing on Mary Douglas and Kristeva on pollution and abjection, and on Deleuze and Guattari's 'becoming-woman' and bodies defined by capacities rather than fixed being, it argues that the female reproductive body is more often barren than fecund and that this state is another generative modality, not an absence. It reads the Western biomedical pathologisation of menopause (Wilson's Feminine Forever, HRT) as a Foucauldian disciplinary discourse, then tracks older women through Sunset Boulevard's Norma Desmond, the hagsploitation cycle (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Strait-Jacket, Hush Hush Sweet Charlotte), and The Taking of Deborah Logan, concluding that Jessica Lange's American Horror Story roles offer the fullest, sexually frank rebuttal to the abjection and invisibility of the ageing woman.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 8. Playing with Glitter
samples.relation: This chapter argues that play is Drag Race's deep structure, developed through three philosophers. Wittgenstein's language games explain the show's word-play: 'realness' subverts its own reference to mean the iconic fake, 'herstory' is history played with from a queer perspective, and lip syncs are rule-following whose rules only exist in application. Gadamer's account of play with 'a life of its own' — requiring willingness and openness to the Other — explains why half-hearted players lose, from Porkchop and Tammie's mouthed-nothing lip sync to Gia Gunn and Trixie breaking character in Snatch Game, and why the Evil Twins and makeover challenges are designed to force queens to open up. Deleuze's rhizome (with Bakhtin's carnivalesque) grounds the claim that drag decentering the human — Lil' Poundcake, dragged pancakes, Sharon Needles — and the finale's carnival dissolve the official binaries of male/female and good/bad.

samples.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
samples.title: As We Wind on Down the Road
samples.relation: Randall Auxier develops a theory, drawn from Ernst Cassirer's work on myth and magic, that distinguishes magic (the generalizing of will so that past, present, and future connect through symbols and co-operating forces) from myth (the consciousness that experiences the world as wills and archetypal symbols). Page embodies the magical path—the zone musicians enter where playing exceeds conscious control, the Faustian need to master it that led him to Crowley, and the risk of being drained (Page in 1977)—while Plant embodies myth, supplying archetypal lyrics ('The Battle of Evermore', 'Kashmir', 'Stairway' as 'a song of hope') and the Welsh pastoral. Zeppelin's blues borrowing is re-enactment rather than repetition, a rhizome-like reinvention of old roots, and the four unpronounceable symbols of the fourth album are genuine creations: symbols that store concentrated will for the future.

samples.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
samples.title: War and Representation
samples.relation: Jameson contends that war poses the 'nominalist dilemma'—the gap between abstract totality and sensory immediacy—making it ultimately unrepresentable, and enumerates eight recurring narrative situations (existential, collective, leaders, technology, landscape, atrocity, homeland attack, occupation). Using Burke's dramatistic pentad he argues the war narrative drifts from 'act/agent' toward 'scene,' where the anthropomorphic dissolves; Sartre's 'groups-in-fusion' and Deleuze's nomadic war machine model the collective buddy-squad, whose division of labor he compares to the heist film. Reading Grimmelshausen's Simplicissimus and Döblin's Wallenstein against Kluge's Stalingrad and Halberstadt collages, he shows war (from the Thirty Years' War to WWII aerial bombing) generating a rhizomatic, nonnarrative flow that defeats stable narrative convention.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: From Sherlock Holmes to the Hard-Boiled Detective in Film Noir
samples.relation: Jerold Abrams argues that the noir detective inherits the Holmes/Dupin detective logic but inhabits a fundamentally different maze. Using Eco's three labyrinths, he maps the classical Greek maze (with faith as Ariadne's string) and the mannerist maze (with Cartesian/Kantian pure reason) onto the escapable world of classic detection, and the Deleuzian rhizomatic maze, born after Nietzsche dissolved reason into will to power, onto noir's inescapable world (The Third Man, Kiss Me Deadly, The Maltese Falcon's fake statue). He shows both detectives use Peircean abduction (the logic of guessing) rather than pure deduction, illustrating it with knife-wound examples and Calloway's trapdoor inference in The Third Man, while the noir femme fatale becomes the anti-Ariadne whose thread of clues leads only to the hangman's rope.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 16. The Truth about the Walkers
samples.relation: Kempner reads the show's serial bait-and-switch over the walkers' origin - Jenner's failed CDC, Eugene's exposed lie on the road to Washington - as an enactment of Deleuze and Guattari's multiplicity against "the reduction to the ONE." Their anti-Oedipal attack on Freud, who fixed the Wolfman's dream to a single castrating father, mirrors how characters who hunt one knowable cause (Rick's hope of CDC rescue, Hershel's barn of curable walkers, Abraham's mission) are punished with death, while Michonne survives precisely by accepting walkers as an irreducible pack rather than something to be understood. The chapter concludes the series should never explain the walkers: multiple causes and small-t truths replace any single Truth, which is why relief never arrives and survival means living with unknowability.

samples.book: 253 - Asimov's Foundation and Philosophy - Psychohistory and Its Discontents
samples.title: 7. History as Creativity
samples.relation: Magomedov reads the Seldon Plan as an 'artificial teleology' imposed on a history that is intrinsically open and contingent: because psychohistory yields only probabilities (Trantor's 92.5 percent, never 100), every Seldon Crisis leaves an infinitesimal gap through which an alternate future can break. Against Aristotelian and Hegelian teleology, he uses Deleuze and Guattari's concepts of territorialization and deterritorialization, plus Nietzsche's idea that a thing's essence is fixed by the forces that seize it, to argue that resolving a crisis requires creativity, and Hardin's inventive balance-of-power solution versus Sermak's stagnant 'attack first' shows Seldon's will surviving only where a force refuses to merely repeat the past.

samples.book: 215 - The Philosophy of the Beats
samples.title: Wholly Communion Poetry, Philosophy, and Spontaneous Bop Cinema
samples.relation: Sterritt reads Peter Whitehead's 1965 film 'Wholly Communion,' shot at London's International Poetry Incarnation, as 'spontaneous bop cinema' embodying Beat poetics through Bakhtin's dialogic/carnivalesque and the schizoanalysis of Deleuze and Guattari. Ginsberg's drunken recitation of 'The Change' becomes a 'body without organs' entering the 'chaosmos' on the plane of immanence; Jandl's sound poetry is pure Deleuzian sensation. Adrian Mitchell's anti-Vietnam 'To Whom It May Concern' is read through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati and Deleuze's 'difference in repetition,' its incantatory counter-words a materialist line of flight against the order-words of war.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reads "The City on the Edge of Forever" through Romanticism: the Guardian of Forever strands Kirk and Spock without historical reference points - a nihilist moment of pure meaninglessness - and Kirk's Romantic response is to rebuild the narrative of the past even at the cost of letting Edith Keeler die. Hegel's philosophy of history explains the compulsion to record (Spock's anguished "I've missed taping centuries of living history"), why Edith's unwitting world-historical role is to die under a truck rather than lead a pacifist America to Nazi conquest, and Novalis's call to "make the world Romantic" frames Spock's self-rescue as young Selek in "Yesteryear". Kirk, Spock, and McCoy become Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy archetypes - Tragic Hero, Apollonian, Dionysian - converging in the street scene where McCoy lunges to save Edith, Spock waits on logic, and Kirk, seizing McCoy's arms, finds a tragic beauty in her death.

samples.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
samples.title: “Howzat!” Prometheus Is a Fast Bowler
samples.relation: Decker argues the Doctor's morality resists formula — his motives are private, his timey-wimey perspective complicates consequentialist calculation, and the 'Genesis of the Daleks' child hypothetical breaks rule theories like Kant's and Mill's — so he reads it as an 'ethics of ambiguity' fusing Romanticism (Shelley's imagination, the infinite glimpsed in cups of tea and small beautiful events, Romantic-Gothic divided consciousness) with Sartrean existentialism. Via Sartre's WWII student, bad faith, and Beauvoir's 'adventurer' contrasted with the sub-man and the serious man, he casts the Doctor as a Gallifreyan Prometheus whose gifts of freedom are both dreadful and delightful.

samples.book: 220 - The Philosophy of David Lynch
samples.title: 9. My Dharma Is the Road that Never Ends
samples.relation: Potter and Cobb argue that Twin Peaks is a Romantic refusal of resolution: mysteries live by not being solved, so Lynch and Frost break the rules that stories need authors, protagonists who solve problems, and endings. They read Cooper's entrapment in a time loop through Nietzsche's eternal recurrence and amor fati (quoting The Gay Science and The Will to Power), tie Wally Brando's Dharma speech and Isaiah Berlin's Roots of Romanticism to the theme, and argue the real 'story' is the endless meta-narrative co-created between the show and each viewer—Life itself as process without endpoint.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 2. Sex Has Something Behind It
samples.relation: John Heaney pairs Louis with Schopenhauer: both see human existence as error-shaped misery, but more importantly both treat sex as the will-to-live tricking the intellect into serving the species while we mistake the species' good for our own. He reads the 'Come on, God' stand-up (every beautiful thought about a woman followed by a disgusting one) and Louie's 'So Old/Playdate' speech that 'sex is really trying to have a family' as comedic versions of Schopenhauer's metaphysics of love, with episodes like 'Bummer/Blueberries' (a decapitation killing Louie's lust mid-non-date), 'Elevator Part 4' (the civil divorce flashback ending in a possible pregnancy), and 'Eddie' (a man losing the will-to-live along with the will-to-love) enacting the oscillation between sexual arousal and suicidal despair. Even Louis's devotion to his daughters fits Schopenhauer's claim that the sexual delusion transfers to offspring, which is why 'Eddie' ends with Louie refusing to name his reasons to live - he has to pick up his kids in the morning.

samples.book: 150 - Black Sabbath and Philosophy - Mastering Reality
samples.title: Black sabbath & philosophy
samples.relation: James Heathers asks why the most improbable band became the one true originator of heavy metal and answers with Schopenhauer: industrial Aston, Birmingham was a monument to the ceaseless, unsatisfied striving of the Will, and music, which maps directly onto the Will itself, gave that world its voice. The tritone's numerically hideous ratios, a point traced through Rameau back to Pythagoras, make it the natural interval of morbidity, which is why "Black Sabbath" and everything from Liszt's Dante Sonata to death metal is marinated in it, and why doom was not a predictable development like Deep Purple or Led Zeppelin. He closes on the irony that Schopenhauer, who preached ascetic denial of the Will, would have loathed a band that answered factory-town despair by smothering the Will in lager, hash, cocaine, and women, only to breed more want in the worst of all possible worlds.

samples.book: 221 - The Philosophy of Film Noir
samples.title: Film Noir and the Meaning of Life
samples.relation: Steven Sanders uses film noir to motivate philosophical reflection on the meaning of life, reading its pessimistic sensibility (Touch of Evil, Detour, Out of the Past, D.O.A., Vertigo) as the presupposition that life is meaningless per se. He runs through Schopenhauer's pessimistic arguments from the vanity and transience of existence, Nagel's rebuttal that our not mattering in a million years does not stop things mattering now, and the tension between Sartrean existentialist freedom and noir's Freudian fatalism of the inescapable past. He then lays out three models of meaninglessness (Baier's worthlessness and purposelessness, Camus/Nagel's absurdity met with irony), reading noir protagonists as ironists, before rejecting the noir view that life must be meaningless and arguing that meaning is a matter of degree, requiring realizable projects of positive value.

samples.book: 175 - Iron Man and Philosophy - Facing the Stark Reality
samples.title: Franken-Stark
samples.relation: Curtis argues Iron Man dramatizes the problem of progress: Schopenhauer's insatiable will explains why every technological fix — the chest plate, the armor, the artificial nervous system — spawns new suffering and dependency, and his pessimism, with Kierkegaard's freedom within insecurity, Nietzsche's flawed Übermensch going out 'in a blaze of glory,' and Sartre's 'cautiously optimistic' existentialism, recasts Iron Man as a tragic antihero rather than a perfected Superman or Batman. Stark's wounded heart, alcoholism as self-medication ('the demon is not in the bottle but in the addict'), and doomed romances with Bethany Cabe and Rumiko Fujikawa make him the flawed hero who has simply learned to live with imperfection. Like Mary Shelley's monster, his extensions have become him — we are all 'Franken-Starks' facing the consequences of our own inventions.

samples.book: 199 - True Detective and Philosophy - A Deeper Kind of Darkness
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues Rust Cohle's stated pessimism and in-principle embrace of suicide closely track Schopenhauer's view that suffering is built into the world with no providential redemption, yet the two diverge because Schopenhauer condemned suicide as an affirmation of the will-to-live rather than its denial. The chapter traces Rust's three-stage arc — jaded wannabe-suicidal pessimist who nonetheless energetically investigates the Dora Lange case, resigned drinker, and finally cautious affirmer of life after the Yellow King confrontation — and contends his detective work is really motivated by a Schopenhauerian morality of compassion and justice, not mere 'programming.' Rust's finale conversion is read as an evidence-based judgment that thoroughgoing pessimism is intellectually dishonest, since compassion and justice do score nontrivial victories.

samples.book: 201 - Veronica Mars and Philosophy - Investigating the Mysteries of Life (Which Is a Bitch Until You Die)
samples.title: Acknowledgment
samples.relation: William Irwin diagnoses Neptune, from the 09-ers down to the PCH-ers, with status anxiety (via Alain de Botton's Status Anxiety) and prescribes the Stoic remedy: Epictetus on the insult lying in our judgment rather than the insulter, and Marcus Aurelius, the emperor who chose serenity over vengeance, show how Keith and Veronica ground self-worth in virtue no one can take away. Sartre's 'hell is other people' and the look explain how Veronica is reduced to a dumb blonde and Duncan to a murderer until he flees to Cuba, while Schopenhauer's choice between loneliness and vulgarity frames Mac's switched-at-birth longing, Wallace's basketball-bought status, and Weevil's self-made standing as PCH leader. Irwin closes by offering the show itself as Aristotelian catharsis-through-comedy, art as therapy for the viewer's own status anxiety.

samples.book: 084 - Leonard Cohen and Philosophy - Various Positions
samples.title: Leonard Cohen and Philosophy
samples.relation: Liane Heller pairs Cohen and Schopenhauer - born and died on September 21st, the autumnal equinox - as two explorers of the world's irrational negativity who both retreat to 'a room' to create. Schopenhauer's directionless Will, his pessimism about a life of constant suffering, his notorious misogyny in 'On Women,' and his ascetic denial of the will-to-live (with his contempt for Judaism and preference for the Upanishads and Buddhist compassion) are set against Cohen's affirmation that love is 'the only engine of survival,' his five-year Zen retreat that could not hold him, and his return to the Judaism of the 'little Jew who wrote the Bible.' A closing imagined dialogue has a humbled Schopenhauer confronted with Cohen's self-compassion and ordinary joys, admitting the limits of his own field of vision.

samples.book: 113 - Jimi Hendrix and Philosophy - Experience Required
samples.title: 3. Mermen and Dismemberment
samples.relation: Contends that Hendrix's discord is philosophy-as-discord: 'I Don't Live Today' (the Native American dead-in-life), the Woodstock 'Star-Spangled Banner' with its bombs and sirens against sporting-event sentimentality, 'Machine Gun,' and 'House Burning Down' lacerate listeners so they actually feel war's atrocities instead of parroting patriotic clichés. Against this the chapter sets the oceanic, womb-like escape fantasies of '1983 (A Merman I Should Turn to Be)' and 'Valleys of Neptune,' treating them through Schopenhauer as metaphysical consolation, Marx's opiate, and Nietzsche's 'hangman's metaphysics,' and concludes that Hendrix finally refuses such world-denying illusions — and Heideggerian inauthentic withdrawal — in favor of existential engagement with suffering here and now.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 77. Journey as Philosophy Meaning, Connection, and the Sublime
samples.relation: Hamer argues Journey works through the interplay of connection, the sublime and meaning. The wordless multiplayer bond with an unnameable stranger before vast vistas dramatizes emotional connection where the ancestors' greed failed. The looming mountain and immense dunes evoke the sublime, read through Burke's pleasurable terror and Kant's mathematical and dynamical sublime (imagination overwhelmed while reason comprehends; feeling power over a nature that cannot harm the deathless player, then rebirth surpassing the sublime into joy). The cyclical return to the start recasts the game as Camus's Myth of Sisyphus: a meaningless repeated ascent that players nonetheless replay, so we must imagine the Traveler — and ourselves — happy to make the beautiful repetition our own.

samples.book: 234 - The Philosophy of Tim Burton
samples.title: The Philosophy of Tim Burton
samples.relation: Jenkins reads Burton's 'Sweeney Todd' (2007) through Edmund Burke's theory of the sublime and the device of synesthesia. She argues Burton relocates Burke's sublime from nature to the man-made, consuming city, staging beauty (Johanna, the flower-market flashbacks, saturated color) in losing tension with the 'dark and gloomy' urban sublime (desaturated Fleet Street, 'Epiphany'). Drawing on German Expressionist visual style (Caligari, Nosferatu) and the raindrop-to-blood credit sequence, she shows how sight, sound and represented taste (Mrs. Lovett's cannibal pies, the jugular-spray 'shooting star' during 'Johanna') mix the senses to force the queasy Burkean confrontation of terror and delight, ending in Burke's nihilistic darkness rather than redemption.

samples.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
samples.title: Top Eleven Contributor Top Ten Lists
samples.relation: Eleven contributor top-ten lists, several applying the book's philosophical tools in miniature: Stone-Mediatore ranks ten songs by how they exemplify Burke's, Kant's, and Longinus's theories of the sublime ('Stairway to Heaven' first), Flynn ranks ten by Nietzsche's Dionysian criterion of celebrating the natural forces that undo us ('When the Levee Breaks' first), and Dick pairs ten songs with Schopenhauer's misogynist essay 'On Women.' The remaining lists — resources, sideman appearances, cover versions, oral fixations, gigs attended — are fanzine fare without philosophical content.

samples.book: 256 - Anthony Bourdain and Philosophy - An Appetite for Life
samples.title: 3. The Nasty Bits
samples.relation: Calef asks how Bourdain could find disgusting foods (cobra heart, blood soup, warthog anus) delicious, using Korsmeyer's taxonomy of disgust and the 'paradox of aversion.' He argues their appeal comes from Aristotelian learning-through-representation, Burke's and Bullough's sublime experienced at psychical distance, and Kristeva's 'abject' — foods that remind us of death and mortality let Bourdain transcend and disarm it by eating them appreciatively.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Walter Barta presents transhumanism as a real philosophy (via Bostrom's history of the movement and 'Why I Want to Be a Posthuman When I Grow Up') that Fallout both practices and indicts: ghouls, FEV super mutants and the Children of the Cathedral, stimpak-Mentat-Jet self-medication, Brotherhood power armor, Mr. House, the Master, Robobrains, John Henry Eden, and Liberty Prime all embody enhancement or post-humanity, and the level-up loop makes every player a transhumanist. Bostrom's transhumanist value of 'the opportunity to explore' maps onto leaving Vault 13 for the open world, but the Red Queen race becomes the game's adaptive-leveling treadmill, and C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man plus Fukuyama's 'Factor-X' warn that optimization can delete what made enhancement worth wanting - as when the Overseer exiles the too-powerful Vault 13 hero and the Enclave President rationalizes genocidal bioweapons ('No price is too high for the survival of the human race'). Existential risk (Toby Ord's Precipice, Bostrom's vulnerable world hypothesis) supplies the final warning: the G.E.C.K.'s energy is also a destruction kit, and the cycle of war repeats until post-humanity or extinction.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 16. Death Becomes Her
samples.relation: Hendrik Kempt reads Drag Race's pervasive death imagery - death-drops, the 'lip sync for your life,' mirror messages, the 'Death Becomes Her' runway - through the philosophy of death. Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' and Stoic self-possession (Ru's 'pay them bitches no mind,' Violet Chachki enduring a tiny corset) explain why elimination, like death, gives no ground for worry once it arrives, while Socrates' 'philosophy is training for death' makes the show a workout video for dying - Socrates even dying fussing over a rooster like a drag mother to Miss Fame. Heidegger's thrownness and being-toward-death set up Sartre's radically free, future-oriented self - so voluntary exits like BenDeLaCreme's self-elimination and Charlie Hides's listless lip-sync betray one's own plans - and Camus's Sisyphus makes Chi Chi DeVayne and Roxxxy Andrews's doomed All Stars returns models of 'acceptance without resignation.' The closing weighs transhumanism's promise of conquered death against a DragCon-forever thought experiment, concluding with Ru's roast eulogy for Lady Bunny that love and irreverence, not immortal life, are the point.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: The Death of Death
samples.relation: Reading Black Mirror's deaths through Bandersnatch's train ending, Be Right Back's AshBot, and San Junipero, the chapter uses Heidegger's presence-at-hand (Stefan's absent mother and rabbit remain present as possibilities he can act on) and Derrida's différance (the meaning of life and death is endlessly deferred as technology scrambles the presence/absence binary - Martha's simulated Ash, Liam's Grain deletions, Chris's guilt-haunted fiancée). A central section frames the whole debate as transhumanism - Kurzweil's three bridges to the posthuman against Fukuyama's warning that self-directed evolution replaces God - before Camus resolves the question of meaning: Kelly and Yorkie, like Sisyphus, create meaning by choosing their fate in a VR heaven that objectively matters nothing. Freud's Eros/Thanatos drives and Epicurus's 'death is nothing to us' close the chapter's question of whether to extend, hasten, or simply accept mortality.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 79. Cyberpunk 2077 as Philosophy Balancing the (Mystical) Ghost in the (Transhuman) Machine
samples.relation: Lay reads Cyberpunk 2077's transhuman Night City against the enhancement debate. Using the Ship of Theseus, Parfit's continuity plus fission/fusion (V and Johnny 'fusing,' the Delamain AIs) and Clark and Chalmers's extended mind, he argues enhancement neither destroys personal identity (which Parfit says doesn't matter) nor dehumanizes users — it may be the purest expression of Clark's cyborg humanity. The real danger is corporate exploitation of bodies, explained via Adorno's culture industry and Arendt's banality of evil. Buddhist nonattachment (Nagarjuna's emptiness, echoed by a Schopenhauer shard) grounds each ending's pacification-versus-attachment theme, but Lay corrects it with Weil's critique of power and Buber's I-Thou, concluding the game urges transcending the boundary between 'me' and 'you' through mystical interpersonal relation.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 16 When Tech Meets Tradition How Wakandan Technology Transcends Anti-Blackness
samples.relation: Timothy Brown argues that transhumanist futures - Bostrom's fable of the Dragon Tyrant, Savulescu's moral bioenhancement, AI built by homogeneous teams - exclude Black people because technologies embed anti-Blackness, from Ruha Benjamin's New Jim Code to facial recognition failing Black women. Black Panther counters this by rooting its future in traumatic memory: Killmonger's museum scene shows how whitewashed 'aesthetic Africanism' licenses incredulity about African technological achievement, while Shuri's comics arc (named 'Ancient Future' by her ancestors in D'Jalia) shows that Wakandan technology flourishes only through the traditions it is tempted to scoff at. Africanfuturism, on this reading, treats Blackness itself as a 'prosthesis' for stress-testing whether the futures we build will include everyone.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Hauskeller argues Shelley's Victor was sane and benevolently motivated, and reads the 'playing God' warning (Whale's 'now I know what it feels to be God!', the Genesis tree of life, the sorcerer's apprentice) as a claim that crossing nature's lines is dangerous rather than sinful. He then flips the story: like the creature, we are children abandoned by a creator who withholds eternal life, so the real wrong is a creator's failure of duty and love - while Epicurus's death-is-nothing-to-us argument and the picture of a childless, static immortal world undermine the transhumanist case that death is the greatest evil. The chapter ends with Aristotle's mean: obsessive pursuit of knowledge and immortality wrecks happiness, which lies in discovering that our native town is the world and living in the present.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Dan Dinello reads the Borg as the nightmare double of Data: where Data embodies Asimov's Laws of Robotics and Federation humanism, the Borg realize Jacques Ellul's and Langdon Winner's thesis that technology is an autonomous, totalitarian force assimilating its makers rather than a neutral tool. He traces the Collective's shared mind and quest for 'perfection' to transhumanism (Max More, James Hughes), whose philosophical roots lie in Descartes's mechanical body and mind-as-information—the very premise of Ira Graves's consciousness upload in 'The Schizoid Man'. Picard's tear as Locutus and Hugh's acquired individuality in 'I, Borg' show that creativity and liberal humanist values, not technology, defeat the ultimate techno-totalitarian dystopia.

samples.book: 263 - Stephen King and Philosophy
samples.title: “Sometimes Dead Is Better”
samples.relation: Katherine Allen reads Pet Sematary and The Tommyknockers as bioconservative fables staging the transhumanism debate: Louis's resurrected, 'fundamentally wrong' cat Church and cannibal son Gage, and Bobbi's tooth-shedding 'New Improved' becoming, dramatize Kass, McKibben and Fukuyama's warning that erasing our limits erases our humanity. Against them she sets Nick Bostrom's 'Fable of the Dragon-Tyrant,' in which death is an unquestioned evil we should slay, and Bernard Williams's worry about the tedium of immortality. King's insistence that 'sometimes dead is better,' and that forbidden knowledge (the Micmac ground, the buried ship) works like an addiction, sides with the deathist view that mortality and finitude give life its meaning.

samples.book: 099 - Louis C.K. and Philosophy - You Don't Get to Be Bored
samples.title: 7. Because Nothing Can’t Be!
samples.relation: Joseph Kirkland takes Louis's 'Why? Why? Why?' routine from One Night Stand - collapsing into 'things that are not can't be!' and 'giant ants with top hats dancing around' - as an accidental encounter with the Pre-Socratics' question of why there is something rather than nothing. Louis, he argues, rejects the Principle of Plenitude (a finite world has no room for every possibility), whereas Parmenides argues from pure logic that nothingness is impossible and change therefore illusory - his student Zeno 'proving' it with paradoxes such as the infinite halfway points between Louis and Ben's Pizzeria. Framing the bit with Plato's claim that wonder is the beginning of philosophy and Socrates' unexamined life, the chapter ends on the parental punchline 'bread first, then ethics': feeding the kid trumps metaphysics, and Louis's frustration comes from failing that duty while his daughter probes being and non-being over her French fries.

samples.book: 273 - Sailing – Philosophy for Everyone - Catching the Drift of Why We Sail
samples.title: SAILING Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: John D. Norton poses three sailing paradoxes — how a wind-powered boat sails into the wind, faster than the wind, and whether 'making its own wind' makes it a perpetual-motion machine — echoing Zeno's paradoxes of motion and measure as engines of philosophical clarity. He resolves the first two by rejecting the causal truism that an effect cannot exceed or oppose its cause (the wind's force, resolved into drive and beam components against a resistant hull, is the real cause), using this to argue causal principles are elastic labels grafted onto science, never laws it must obey. For the third he builds an idealized wind-turbine boat thought experiment showing created-wind energy is exactly consumed by counter-force, and debates James Brown's Platonist view (that thought experiments 'see' laws in a Platonic realm, like grasping the ideal triangle) against his own deflationary view that they are merely picturesque argument.

samples.book: 153 - Disney and Philosophy - Truth, Trust, and a Little Bit of Pixie Dust
samples.title: Happily Ever After
samples.relation: Runs Descartes' dreaming argument and evil-genius doubt on Aurora, for whom the scenario is literal: Maleficent is an actually existing deceiver who could have enchanted her whole life in a dungeon. G. E. Moore's common-sense proof — 'here is a hand,' dubbed the Pinocchio test after the real boy — and the Moorean shift answer the skeptic, illustrated by Maleficent deploying Zeno's paradox to stop Prince Phillip's sword, where Phillip rightly clings to the more certain premise that motion is possible. Nozick's experience machine explains why Aurora should care: we want to actually be good and live real lives rather than merely experience them, so authentic 'happily ever after' requires knowing our experiences are backed by reality.

samples.book: 045 - World of Warcraft and Philosophy - Wrath of the Philosopher King
samples.title: Which World Am I In
samples.relation: Juan Ferret tells the story from inside the game: Admetus the Human Mage, chased through Alterac Valley by an Undead Rogue, works through Zeno's paradox of motion, the convergence of infinite series, and whether space and time are discrete, coached by a bodiless voice that turns out to be his player. The voice's revelations — 'You are my creation,' autorun, polymorph, Blink — force the free-will-versus-determinism question from the character's side, since every action is controlled from above. Reference frames, Heisenberg's uncertainty, EPR entanglement, and hidden nods to David Lewis ('Siwel Divad' on possible worlds) and many-worlds theory leave the mage wondering which world, server, or parallel universe he really inhabits.

samples.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
samples.title: Deleuze Jam Today
samples.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

samples.book: 055 - Doctor Who and Philosophy - Bigger on the Inside
samples.title: We Wouldn’t Be Here Without Time Travel
samples.relation: Worley distinguishes logical from empirical possibility (Leonardo's round-square in 'City of Death') and shows that time-travel paradoxes — Leela's self-caused antibodies, the unauthored 'Blink' Easter egg, the Master's Toclafane — can be handled with Zeno-style analysis of contradiction and David Lewis's distinction between external and personal time, under which travelers instantiate rather than rewrite history ('The Visitation', 'The Time Meddler'). He then reads 'Turn Left' and the Doctor's 'alternative time' in 'Pyramids of Mars' through Leibniz's possible worlds and Lewis's actualism about parallel universes, concluding that in 'City of Death' time travel is essential to life on Earth existing at all.

samples.book: 244 - The Who and Philosophy
samples.title: We Wouldn’t Be Here Without Time Travel
samples.relation: Peter Worley finishes the Doctor's "wibbly-wobbly" speech from "Blink" by distinguishing empirical from logical possibility (via a fictional chat with Leonardo about a round-square) and asking whether time travel is coherent. Using "The Edge of Destruction," "The Aztecs," "The Visitation," and "Turn Left," he deploys David Lewis's external-versus-personal time distinction and Lewis's rule that a time traveler's acts must be the very events that made history, then treats the Doctor and Lewis as "actualists" about possible worlds to dissolve grandfather-style paradoxes and time loops.
